data.value: Actions that take effect at once

data.name: Help.Panel.KeySearch
data.value: Search pages, go to the menu

data.name: Help.Panel.KeyEnter
data.value: Saves in a side panel (actions you can take back)

data.name: Help.Panel.KeyChord

data.name: Tour.WORKCENTER.Step1.Text
data.value: Inbox holds work and approval requests sent to you, My Work the work you own, and Pool the work your team can pick up.

data.name: Tour.WORKCENTER.Step2.Text
data.value: Type part of a title to narrow the list; the filter chips narrow it further by type and status.

data.name: Tour.WORKCENTER.Step3.Text
data.value: Click a row to open the work: its details, checklist, comments and history are there.

data.name: Tour.WORKCENTER.Step4.Text
data.value: Accept, Start and Complete sit on the row. Open an approval request to Approve or Reject it; to hand work to someone else, use Delegate in the opened work.

data.name: Tour.WORKCENTER.Step5.Text
data.value: Create a new task, note or meeting from here.

data.name: Tour.MYTIMESHEET.Step1.Text
data.value: Move between weeks with the arrows; Today brings you back to the current week.

data.name: Tour.MYTIMESHEET.Step2.Text
data.value: Use + Task row or + Category row to add what you worked on this week.

data.name: Tour.MYTIMESHEET.Step3.Text
data.value: Type the hours into each day's cell; the totals update as you go.

data.name: Tour.MYTIMESHEET.Step4.Text
data.value: When the week is complete, choose Submit for approval; your approver then sees it in Timesheet approvals.

data.name: Tour.TIMEAPPROVALS.Step1.Text
data.value: Weeks your team submitted for approval are listed here.

data.name: Tour.TIMEAPPROVALS.Step2.Text
data.value: Open a row to read the week, then choose Approve, or Return with a reason so it can be corrected.

data.name: Help.USERS.Purpose
data.value: Manage everyone who can sign in to your tenant: invite users, edit their details and decide whether each account is active.

data.name: Help.USERS.Step1
data.value: Narrow the list with the search box, or click “Filter”, choose “Status”, “Roles” or “Account Type” and click “Apply”.

data.name: Help.USERS.Step2
data.value: Click “Add User”, fill in “Email”, “First Name” and “Last Name” in the side panel, then click “Save” or press Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac). An invitation e-mail is sent, so a bare Enter does not save.

data.name: Help.USERS.Step3
data.value: Ask the new user to set a password through the e-mailed link; until then the status shows “Invited” and the row offers “Resend Invitation”.

data.name: Help.USERS.Step4
data.value: Open a row's actions to “View” or “Edit” a user, “Disable” or “Enable” the account, send a “Reset Password” link, or “Delete” it.

data.name: Help.USERS.Step5
data.value: To give a user roles, open the User Roles page; the “Roles” column here only shows what is already assigned.

data.name: Help.USERS.Related.ROLES
data.value: To see what each role allows

data.name: Help.ROLES.Purpose
data.value: This page lists your tenant's roles: System roles that come with the platform and Custom roles you create.

data.name: Help.ROLES.Step1
data.value: Search the list, or click “Filter”, pick “System (built-in, locked)” or “Custom (editable)” under “Type” and click “Apply”.

data.name: Help.ROLES.Step2
data.value: Click “Add Role”, enter “Name” and “Display Name” (and a “Description” if needed), then click “Save”; the name cannot be changed later.

data.name: Help.ROLES.Step3
data.value: Click the key icon “Manage Permissions” on a row to open Role Permissions with that role already selected.

data.name: Help.ROLES.Step4
data.value: Use “View”, “Edit” or “Delete” on a custom role; a system role shows a lock icon and can only be viewed.

data.name: Help.ROLES.Related.ROLEPERMISSIONS
data.value: To set what a role may do

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Purpose
data.value: This page sets what a role is allowed to do: you grant or remove permissions, grouped by module, for one role at a time.

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Step1
data.value: Pick a role in the “Role” box; coming from “Manage Permissions” on the Roles page opens it with the role already selected.

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Step2
data.value: Narrow the permissions with “Module”, the “Search permissions…” box, or the “All”, “Assigned” and “Unassigned” tabs.

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Step3
data.value: Click an unassigned permission chip to grant it to the role; the change is saved at once.

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Step4
data.value: Click an assigned chip and confirm to remove it; chips with a lock come from the baseline or a module and cannot be changed here.

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Step5
data.value: Check “Selected Role” on the right for “Permission coverage” and the assigned, locked and unassigned counts.

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Immediate
data.value: Granting and removing a permission; it affects every user who holds the role

data.name: Help.USERROLES.Purpose
data.value: This page links users to roles: pick one user, then give them roles or take roles away.

data.name: Help.USERROLES.Step1
data.value: Pick a person in the “User” box to see the roles they hold and the ones they do not.

data.name: Help.USERROLES.Step2
data.value: Narrow the roles with the “Search Roles” box or the “All”, “Assigned” and “Unassigned” tabs.

data.name: Help.USERROLES.Step3
data.value: Click “Assign” on a role under “Unassigned Roles” to give it to the user; the change is saved at once.

data.name: Help.USERROLES.Step4
data.value: Click “Remove” on an assigned role, or the x beside it under “Active Roles”, and confirm to take it away.

data.name: Help.USERROLES.Immediate
data.value: Assigning and removing a role; a user gets the permissions of all their roles together

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Purpose
data.value: This page lists the items (materials kept in stock: active ingredients, excipients, packaging, intermediates) with their identity, material type and stock behaviour. Each item is created here and taken through its statuses: “Draft”, “Awaiting approval”, “Active”, “Deactivated”, “Retired”.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step1
data.value: Narrow the list with the search box, or click “Filter”, choose “Status” or “Material type” and click “Apply”.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step2
data.value: Click “Add item”, fill in the identity and the stock behaviour on its full-page form, then click “Save”: the item is saved as “Draft”. In a single-line field of that form, Enter saves it too (in the “Description” box Enter starts a new line). Later, on an active item only the name and the description change freely; a filled stock field needs an approved correction.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step3
data.value: Open a draft's “Actions” and choose “Send for approval”: the item stays “Awaiting approval” until it is approved, and only then becomes “Active”. While it is awaiting approval, the person who sent the request can choose “Withdraw Approval Request” in its “Actions”: the item goes back to its previous status.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step4
data.value: “Deactivate” takes an active item out of new stock entries; “Request reactivation” goes through the same approval again; “Retire” is final, is allowed only for a deactivated item with zero stock, and the code is never reused. Each of them asks for a reason.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step5
data.value: Outside a text field, with no dialog or side panel open, the “?” key opens this help with the page's shortcuts.

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Purpose
data.value: Set the evidence a rep must give when starting a visit: location, photo, institution QR code and device verification. The tenant setting applies to every rep; a time-boxed exception relaxes a rule for one rep for a while.

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step1
data.value: On the “Scoped settings” tab, make a choice for each kind of evidence in the “Setting form”. The preview on the right shows what the rep will see when starting a visit.

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step2
data.value: Click “Save”, check the changed rows and confirm with “Save and apply”. The setting applies to every rep at once.

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step3
data.value: “Change history” shows who changed what and when. “Reps” shows each rep's value in force today; a value relaxed by an exception is marked “exception”.

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step3Title
data.value: Follow the history and the reps

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step4
data.value: On the “Time-boxed exceptions” tab, click “New exception”. Enter the rep, the rules to relax, a date range of at most 30 days and the reason, then click “Send for approval” or press Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac).

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step5
data.value: The exception is approved in the Task Center; the requester cannot approve their own. Only an approved exception within its dates applies. In the quick view, “Cancel exception” and “End early” ask for a reason; type it and confirm with Ctrl+Enter.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Purpose
data.value: Review the evidence flags of started visits: a far or missing location, a short visit, a QR code not scanned or invalid, a start under an exception. A flag is a hint to look into; on its own it does not mean a rule was broken.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Audience
data.value: Area managers and the sales operations team

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step1
data.value: For “Period”, choose “Last 7 days”, “Last 30 days” or “Custom range…”. A custom range can be at most 92 days.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step2
data.value: Filter by “Rep”, “Institution” and flag type. “Flagged only” is on; turn it off to list visits without flags too.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step3
data.value: The cards on top show “Visits started”, “Flagged visits” and “By flag type”. One visit can carry several flags.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step4
data.value: The row's quick view shows the location, the distance to the institution, the QR code result and any exception; seeing the photo needs its own permission. “Open the visit” opens the visit itself.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step5
data.value: The “Rep summary” tab shows started and flagged visits per rep, the rate and the most frequent flag. Clicking a row filters the visit list to that rep.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Purpose
data.value: Manage the QR codes posted at the institutions' reception desks. The rep scans this code when starting a visit; a sub-unit without its own code uses its parent institution's code.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Immediate
data.value: Generating, regenerating and revoking a code

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step1
data.value: Filter the list by “Region”, “City”, “Institution type” and “QR status”. “Last scan” and “Last 30 days” show whether the code is in use.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step2
data.value: Select rows and run “Generate for selected (those without a code)”; institutions that already have an active code are skipped. Up to 200 institutions can be selected at a time.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step3
data.value: Print one code with the row's “Print the code” and several with “Print selected (label sheet)”. On the print page, choose “Single” or “Label sheet” and click “Print”.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step4
data.value: On the institution's page, use “Regenerate” or “Revoke” on the “Institution QR code” card. Both make the posted and printed old codes invalid at once; revoking asks for a reason.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step5
data.value: Whether the code is required or optional is the “Institution QR code” setting on the Visit Evidence page. Under the required setting, a visit started at an institution without a code is flagged.

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Purpose
data.value: Set the limits that class a doctor's monthly patient count in a product's indications as Low, Medium or High. A product row comes before the tenant default; when neither exists, the built-in values apply.

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step1
data.value: On the “Thresholds” tab, the “Tenant default” row stays on top in every sort order; product rows take precedence over it. The “Source” column shows where a value comes from.

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step2
data.value: The row's “Edit” action opens the side panel. Enter “Low below (X)” and “High above (Y)”; try a monthly patient count in the preview to see its class.

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step3
data.value: Click “Save” or press Enter; check the changed values and confirm with “Yes, save”. The change takes effect at once.

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step4
data.value: For a product that needs limits different from the default, open its own row with “Add product”.

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step5
data.value: The “Change history” tab shows every change with the person, the row and the old → new value; the list can be exported as CSV or Excel.

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Purpose
data.value: Write approved answers to the objections a rep may hear from a doctor during a visit. An approved answer is chosen as an expected objection in knowledge path steps and appears in the rep's notes during the presentation.

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step1
data.value: Narrow the list by “Product”, “Category” and “Status”, or search the objection text.

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step2
data.value: Click “New objection response”; fill in “Product”, “Category”, “Objection · the doctor’s question” and “Approved answer”, choose supporting claims from the product's approved claims and click “Save draft”.

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step3
data.value: “Send for approval” locks the answer during review; “Withdraw” returns it to draft.

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step4
data.value: The approver chooses “Approve”, or writes a note and chooses “Return to draft”. The person who wrote or sent the answer cannot approve it.

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step5
data.value: An approved answer cannot be changed; open a new draft with “New draft from copy”. “Retire” drops the answer from every presentation at once and cannot be undone; “Where it is used” shows which steps are affected.

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Purpose
data.value: Manage the products reps choose as competitors in their reports: company, active ingredient, the products of ours they compete with, and price and reimbursement per country.

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Audience
data.value: Master data and sales operations teams

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step1
data.value: Filter by “Our product”, “Company”, “Active ingredient”, “Country” or “Status”; the search also covers other names.

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step2
data.value: Click “New competitor product”; enter the name, company, active ingredient and at least one of our products, write the box price and reimbursement on the country rows and click “Save”. “Rep view” shows the card the rep will see in the report.

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step3
data.value: On the “Rep proposals” tab, new competitors written by reps in their reports are waiting. With “Decision”, prepare a complete, merge or reject decision and click “Send for approval”.

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step4
data.value: The decision applies once it is approved in the Task Center; whoever prepared it cannot approve it. Until then, the proposal is used only in the proposing rep's reports.

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step5
data.value: The details page shows “Usage in reports” and “Change history”. “Merge with another record” links the record to another one after approval and cannot be undone; “Deactivate” makes it unselectable in new reports.

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Purpose
data.value: Plan, visit and report your week in one calendar. When you start a visit, the evidence the tenant asks for (location, photo, institution QR code) is taken; the report is sent within 48 hours.

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Immediate
data.value: Approving the week, starting a visit, sending a report

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step1
data.value: Switch to “Plan” mode; drag target doctors onto a day or a time. Add products to an institution's planned doctors with “Apply products”.

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step2
data.value: When the plan is ready, click “Approve the week”. An approved week is read-only; to change it, use “Reopen the week” with a reason.

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step3
data.value: In “Execute” mode, open today's visit and click “Start visit” when you arrive at the institution. Depending on the setting, a photo, the location and the “Institution QR code” are asked for; then “Start presentation” opens the presentation.

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step4
data.value: After the visit, click “Send the report”. You have 48 hours for the report; after that the record is locked.

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step5
data.value: For a visit that did not take place, choose “Not done” or “Reschedule” and give the reason. You can add an unplanned visit for today with “Unplanned visit”.
